chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about the man who makes it upon himself for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, the fasting of a specified day. He said: 'He should fast it always, during travel and residence.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who vows to fast on a specific day of the week?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the ruling for a specific vow (*nadhr*) to fast on a designated day, ruling that the obligation is perpetual and binding in both travel (*safar*) and residence (*hadr*). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that specific time-bound vows do not automatically inherit the general exemptions of travel, distinguishing them from general voluntary fasts. It underscores the seriousness of fulfilling one's word to Allah, a principle deeply rooted in Shia legal theory regarding vows.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who Made it upon himself for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, Fasting of a specified day. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should be Fasting it for ever, during the journey and the presence (at home)’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who places upon himself for Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, fasting of a definite day.
He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to fast definitely, regardless of being on a journey or at home.’”
